mainTopic: Making a גוי's winepress and wine vessels usable: ניגוב, קילוף, and vessels that store wine (קיום)
overview: The משנה gives three rules for a winepress that a גוי coated with pitch. A stone press only needs cleansing (ניגוב). For a wooden press, רבי says cleansing is enough and חכמים require peeling the pitch off (קילוף). An earthenware press stays forbidden even after peeling. רבא's teaching on the משנה comes in two opposite versions about a press the גוי also trod grapes in. A story shows רב finding a hidden crack full of wine in a smooth press, so he required peeling. A ברייתא then teaches that רבי allows wiping a press, ladle and funnel, but agrees that jugs are forbidden because they hold wine for storage (קיום). The גמרא settles two clashes between the ברייתא and the משנה: one by whether the גוי trod in the press, and one by saying the end of the משנה follows חכמים. רבא rules that a wine tank must be scalded, and that anything storing wine even briefly falls under the decree. The amud ends by asking whether wiping is done with water or with ashes, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A stone winepress lined with pitch only needs cleansing
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a stone winepress coated with pitch by a גוי becomes permitted after cleansing.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a גוי coated a stone winepress with pitch, you clean it off and it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with the easiest case: a stone winepress that a גוי coated with pitch. Cleaning it is enough to make it usable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stone is hard and does not soak in much wine. So even though the גוי's wine touched the pitch, a simple cleansing (ניגוב) is enough, and wine pressed in it afterward is permitted.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A winepress of stone
that a gentile lined with pitch,
phrases.notes: After lining it, the גוי would pour wine on the pitch to take away the pitch taste. That is how forbidden wine gets onto it.

phrases.english: one cleanses it, and it is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ גַּת שֶׁל אֶבֶן שֶׁזְּפָתָהּ גּוֹי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stone press lined with pitch by a גוי is permitted after ניגוב.

steps.title: A wooden winepress: cleansing or peeling?
steps.stepSummary: רבי says a wooden press only needs cleansing. חכמים say the pitch must be peeled off.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a wooden press, רבי says: clean it. The חכמים say: peel off the pitch.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a wooden winepress, and here there is a disagreement. רבי says cleaning is enough, while חכמים require removing the pitch completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wood absorbs more than stone, so חכמים worry that wine soaked into the pitch and the wood. רבי treats wood like stone, so cleansing is enough. חכמים demand the stronger step of קילוף.

phrases.english: And one of wood,
Rabbi says: One cleanses it,
and the Rabbis say: One must peel off the pitch.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from stone to wood, where there is a disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wooden press: רבי says ניגוב is enough; חכמים require קילוף.

steps.title: An earthenware winepress stays forbidden
steps.stepSummary: An earthenware press remains forbidden even after the pitch is peeled off.
steps.simpleTranslation: For an earthenware press, even if the pitch was peeled off, it is still forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with the strictest case. An earthenware winepress cannot be fixed, even by peeling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earthenware soaks up liquid deeply. Removing the pitch does not take out the wine absorbed into the clay itself. So the order goes stone (cleanse), then wood (argued), then clay (forbidden).
steps.whatToRemember: Stone: cleanse it. Wood: רבי says cleanse, חכמים say peel. Earthenware: forbidden even after peeling.

phrases.english: And one of earthenware,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁקָּלַף אֶת הַזֶּפֶת —
phrases.english: even if one peeled off the pitch,
this is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁל חֶרֶס, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁקָּלַף אֶת הַזֶּפֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list with the strictest material.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An earthenware press stays forbidden even after קילוף.

steps.title: רבא: only a press lined with pitch needs cleansing
steps.stepSummary: In his first version, רבא says the משנה's cleansing rule applies only when the press was lined with pitch, not when the גוי just trod grapes in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This applies only when he lined it with pitch. But if he only trod grapes in it, cleansing is not needed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא limits the משנה. Cleansing is required only when the גוי coated the press with pitch. If he only pressed grapes in it, no cleansing is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pitch is what traps the wine on the surface. Without pitch, simply treading grapes in a stone press does not create the same problem, so רבא says nothing is required.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rava says:
Specifically when he lined it with pitch;
but if he trod grapes in it, not.
phrases.notes: He means cleansing is not needed at all when there was no pitch.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how far the משנה's case reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cleansing is required only for a press lined with pitch; a press that was only trodden in needs nothing.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious from the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא needed to say this, since the משנה already says 'lined it with pitch.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this obvious? We learned 'lined it with pitch'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא: the משנה already speaks only about pitch, so what did he add?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is that רבא's statement seems unnecessary. If the משנה's words already limit the case to pitch, saying 'only pitch' teaches nothing new.

phrases.english: It is obvious! We learned 'lined it with pitch'!

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's wording already limits the case to pitch, so רבא seems to add nothing.

steps.title: Without רבא, we might think 'pitch' was just the usual case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we might have thought the משנה mentioned pitch only because that is what usually happens. רבא teaches that pitch really matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said the same applies even if he only trod in it, and the משנה said 'pitch' only because that is the normal way. So רבא teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא. The משנה's words alone could have been read as just describing the typical situation, so רבא had to say that pitch is the real condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה often describes the usual case without meaning to exclude others. רבא shows that here 'pitch' is a real condition: without it, no cleansing is needed.

phrases.aramaic: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: הוּא הַדִּין אֲפִילּוּ דָּרַךְ בָּהּ,
phrases.english: Lest you say: the same is true even if he trod grapes in it,
and the fact that it teaches 'lined it with pitch'
is because it teaches the usual way of things,
so he teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: הוּא הַדִּין אֲפִילּוּ דָּרַךְ בָּהּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the statement is needed to block a mistaken reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's 'pitch' is just the usual case, so even treading alone would require cleansing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Pitch is a real condition; treading alone needs no cleansing.

steps.title: Second version: if he also trod in it, cleansing is not enough
steps.stepSummary: Another version of רבא: cleansing works only when the press was just lined with pitch. If the גוי also trod grapes in it, cleansing is not enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רבא said: Only when he lined it with pitch. But if he trod grapes in it, cleansing is not enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, opposite version of רבא's teaching. Here treading makes the case stricter, not more lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, a press that was actually used for treading has wine pressed into it under force. So the simple ניגוב that works for a press that was only lined is not enough, and more is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not enough for it

steps.confusionAlert: The two versions point in opposite directions. In the first, treading is more lenient (no cleansing needed). In the second, treading is stricter (cleansing is not enough).

phrases.english: There are those who say: Rava says:
Specifically when he lined it with pitch;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל דָּרַךְ בָּהּ לָא סַגִּי לַהּ בְּנִיגּוּב.
phrases.english: but if he trod grapes in it, cleansing is not enough for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposite version of רבא's teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cleansing works only for a press that was only lined with pitch; a press that was also trodden in needs more than ניגוב.

steps.title: Again: isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The same challenge is raised against the second version.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this obvious? We learned 'lined it with pitch'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats its challenge, now aimed at the second version of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה allows cleansing only in a case of pitch, then of course a press that was also trodden in is not covered. So רבא seems to add nothing.

phrases.english: It is obvious! We learned 'lined it with pitch'!

steps.kashyaTarget: The second version of רבא in step 7
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's wording already limits cleansing to pitch, so the statement seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Otherwise we'd think cleansing works even after treading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that without רבא we might think the leniency of cleansing also covers a press that was trodden in.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said the same applies even if he trod in it, and the משנה said 'pitch' only because that is the usual way. So he teaches us: only pitch, and if he trod in it, cleansing is not enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the second version the same way. It spells out רבא's full point again: cleansing helps only for a press that was just lined.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mistaken thought would be that 'pitch' is just the usual case, so cleansing would also be enough after treading. רבא blocks that leniency.
steps.whatToRemember: Both versions use the same 'obvious? no, you might have thought it was just the usual case' pattern, but they reach opposite results about a trodden press.

phrases.aramaic: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: הוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ דָּרַךְ בָּהּ,
phrases.english: Lest you say: the same is true even if he trod grapes in it,
and the fact that it teaches 'lined it with pitch'
is because it teaches the usual way of things,
so he teaches us: specifically when he lined it with pitch,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל דָּרַךְ בָּהּ לָא סַגִּי לַהּ בְּנִיגּוּב.
phrases.english: but if he trod grapes in it, cleansing is not enough for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: הוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ דָּרַךְ בָּהּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the statement is needed to block a mistaken leniency
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Cleansing would be enough even after treading, since 'pitch' is just the usual case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Cleansing is limited to a press that was only lined; a trodden press needs more.

steps.title: A man asks רבי חייא for someone to purify his winepress
steps.stepSummary: A story is brought that fits the second version: רבי חייא sends רב to purify a man's winepress and warns him to be careful.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like that man who came before רבי חייא and said: Give me a man to purify my winepress. רבי חייא said to רב: Go with him, and make sure people don't complain about me in the study hall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that matches רבא's second version. This step sets up the scene; the lesson comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא warns רב not to be too lenient, so that people in the בית מדרש will not criticize רבי חייא for permitting something forbidden. This hints that the job needs careful checking.

keyTerms.meaning: You cause (people) to cry out, complain

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא,
phrases.english: Like that man who came before Rabbi Ḥiyya,
he said to him: Give me a man
who will purify my winepress for me.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean 'who will purify.'

phrases.english: He said to Rav: Go with him,

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲזִי דְּלָא מְצַוְּחַתְּ עֲלַי בֵּי מִדְרְשָׁא.
phrases.english: and see that you do not cause people to complain about me in the study hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story that fits the second version of רבא.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's second version: a press that was used for wine needs more than ניגוב
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב purifying a winepress for רבי חייא

steps.title: רב first thinks cleansing is enough
steps.stepSummary: רב sees the press is very smooth and thinks ניגוב will be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and saw it was very smooth. He said: This certainly only needs cleansing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב looks at the press and, because it is so smooth, first decides that a simple cleansing will work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A very smooth surface seems not to absorb anything, so ניגוב looks like enough. This first impression sets up the surprise in the next step.

phrases.english: He went and saw that it was very smooth,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: הָא וַדַּאי בְּנִיגּוּב סַגִּי לַהּ.
phrases.english: he said: For this, cleansing is certainly enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב inspects the press.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's first assessment: a smooth press needs only ניגוב.

steps.title: A hidden crack full of wine: peeling is needed
steps.stepSummary: רב finds a crack full of wine, decides peeling is required, and understands his uncle's warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: As he walked back and forth, he saw a crack under him full of wine. He said: Cleansing is not enough here, only peeling. This is what my uncle meant: make sure people don't complain about me in the study hall.
steps.whatsHappening: רב discovers wine soaked into a crack beneath the surface and changes his ruling to require קילוף. Now he understands why רבי חייא warned him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A press that was used for wine can hold wine in hidden places even when it looks smooth. This matches רבא's second version: once a press was used for treading, ניגוב is not enough. רבי חייא's warning was really about this kind of hidden problem.
steps.whatToRemember: A press that looks smooth may still hold forbidden wine in hidden cracks. A press that was used for wine needs קילוף, not just ניגוב.

phrases.english: While he was going back and forth,
he saw a crack underneath him
and saw that it was full of wine,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: הָא לָא סַגִּי לַהּ בְּנִיגּוּב אֶלָּא בְּקִילּוּף,
phrases.english: he said: For this, cleansing is not enough, only peeling,
and this is what my uncle meant when he said to me:

phrases.aramaic: חֲזִי דְּלָא מְצַוְּחַתְּ עֲלַי בֵּי מִדְרְשָׁא.
phrases.english: See that you do not cause people to complain about me in the study hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּהֲדֵי דְּקָא אָזֵיל וְאָתֵי, חֲזָא פִּילָא מִתּוּתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses רב's first assessment after a closer look.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A press that was used for wine, with wine absorbed in hidden places, needs קילוף and not just ניגוב. This supports רבא's second version.

steps.title: A ברייתא: רבי permits a gentile's winepress tools by wiping, the חכמים forbid
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a dispute about a gentile's winepress, ladle and funnel.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: a gentile's winepress, ladle and funnel. רבי allows them after wiping them clean, and the חכמים forbid them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about cleaning a gentile's winepress and the tools used with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds that wiping is enough for these items. The חכמים hold that wiping does not make them usable. The rest of this section builds on this dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: A ladle used to scoop wine

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The winepress, the ladle and the funnel that belong to gentiles,
רבי permits them by wiping,
and the Sages forbid them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא on the same topic of purifying a gentile's winepress.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: wiping makes the winepress, ladle and funnel permitted. חכמים: they stay forbidden.

steps.title: רבי agrees that gentiles' jugs are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that רבי agrees jugs cannot be fixed by wiping.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי agrees that gentiles' jugs are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא shows that רבי's leniency has a limit: jugs stay forbidden, even according to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי allowed wiping for the press tools, but not for jugs. This raises an obvious question, and the ברייתא asks it next.

phrases.english: And רבי agrees regarding jugs belonging to gentiles
that they are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי's leniency from step 13.

steps.title: Why are jugs different from the press tools?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what difference separates jugs from the ladle and funnel.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between this and that?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a question to set up its own explanation, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both kinds of items touch the gentile's wine. So why can the ladle and funnel be wiped, while the jugs cannot?

phrases.english: And what is the difference between this and that?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the distinction made in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason jugs are forbidden while the ladle and funnel can be wiped.

steps.title: Jugs hold wine for storage; the ladle and funnel do not
steps.stepSummary: Storage is the key: a jug keeps the wine inside it, while the tools only pass it along.
steps.simpleTranslation: A jug holds the wine for storage. The ladle and funnel do not hold it for storage.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. Holding wine for storage is what makes the difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine sitting in a jug for a long time soaks into it, so wiping cannot fix it. A ladle or funnel only touches the wine briefly, so wiping is enough for רבי.
steps.whatToRemember: The idea of קיום (holding wine for storage) is the key test. רבא comes back to it at the end of this section.

phrases.english: This one holds it for storage,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the jug, and "it" is the wine.

phrases.english: and that one does not hold it for storage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Jugs store wine and the press tools do not. Storage is what makes an item forbidden even for רבי.

steps.title: Wood and stone are wiped, but pitch-lined ones are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying wood or stone items are wiped, but forbidden if lined with pitch.
steps.simpleTranslation: Items of wood or of stone: one wipes them. If they were lined with pitch, they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives one more rule: plain wood or stone gets wiped, but a pitch lining makes the item forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pitch soaks up wine. So a pitch-lined item is treated more strictly than bare wood or stone. The גמרא is about to challenge this from the משנה.

phrases.english: And those of wood and of stone: one wipes them,
and if they were lined with pitch, they are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא with a rule about materials.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wood or stone: wiping is enough. Lined with pitch: forbidden.

steps.title: Challenge: the משנה lets you wipe a pitch-lined stone press
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a stone press lined with pitch can be wiped, which seems to clash with the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: a stone winepress that a gentile lined with pitch can be wiped, and it is pure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the end of the ברייתא using our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says pitch-lined items are forbidden. The משנה says a pitch-lined stone press only needs wiping. The two sources seem to say opposite things.

keyTerms.meaning: That he lined it with pitch

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in the Mishnah:
a stone winepress that a gentile lined with pitch,
one wipes it and it is pure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the pitch rule of step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that pitch-lined items are forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says a pitch-lined stone press is made pure by wiping. That contradicts the ברייתא.

steps.title: The משנה is where he did not tread grapes; the ברייתא is where he did
steps.stepSummary: The two sources speak about different cases: whether the gentile trod grapes in the press.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה speaks of a press he did not tread in. The ברייתא speaks of one he did tread in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each source is talking about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the gentile only lined the press with pitch and never trod grapes in it, wiping is enough. If he actually trod grapes in it, the pitch lining makes it forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה itself

phrases.english: The Mishnah is where he did not tread in it,
phrases.notes: "Tread" means stomping grapes to make wine inside the press.

phrases.english: the baraita is where he did tread in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (each source speaks about a different situation)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought both sources spoke about the same pitch-lined press.
steps.terutzMaskana: Without treading, wiping is enough. With treading, the pitch-lined press is forbidden.

steps.title: Quoting the ברייתא's dispute again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening of the ברייתא again to examine it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: a gentile's winepress, ladle and funnel. רבי permits them by wiping, and the חכמים forbid them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the first line of the ברייתא. This sets up a new challenge, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the focus moves to the dispute itself: רבי permits by wiping. The גמרא is about to ask whom our משנה follows.

phrases.english: The Master said:
The winepress, the ladle and the funnel that belong to gentiles,
רבי permits them by wiping, and the Sages forbid them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא's opening line (step 13) to start a new challenge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Restates that רבי permits by wiping and the חכמים forbid.

steps.title: Challenge: the משנה forbids an earthenware press even after peeling
steps.stepSummary: The משנה forbids an earthenware press even after peeling the pitch. Can that fit רבי, who permits by wiping alone?
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned: an earthenware press, even if he peeled off the pitch, is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's report of רבי's view, using the end of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is very strict about earthenware. Even peeling (קליפה), which is more than wiping, does not help. According to the ברייתא, רבי allows a press with mere wiping, so the משנה seems to go against רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned (opens a challenge from a משנה)

phrases.english: But didn't we learn:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל חֶרֶס, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁקָּלַף אֶת הַזֶּפֶת —
phrases.english: one of earthenware, even if he peeled off the pitch,
it is forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the restated dispute of step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's lenient view that wiping a press is enough.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה forbids an earthenware press even after peeling, which is stricter than רבי's view.

steps.title: רבא: the end of the משנה follows the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the last part of the משנה matches the חכמים, not רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: in the end of the משנה, we have arrived at the view of the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא solves the clash by saying the end of the משנה follows the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no contradiction with רבי, because the strict last line of the משנה is the view of the חכמים. The חכמים are the ones who forbid.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה
We have come to the view of the Rabbis

phrases.english: Rava said:
In the last clause of the Mishnah we have arrived at the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the clause to a different author
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the whole משנה followed רבי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The strict earthenware line follows the חכמים.

steps.title: רבא: a wine tank must be scalded
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that a gentile's wine tank is fixed by scalding it with hot water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: a wine tank, scald it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new rule: a tank used for gentiles' wine needs scalding, not just wiping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tank holds wine for storage. So, following the rule of קיום from step 16, simple wiping is not enough.

phrases.english: Rava taught:
A wine tank: scald it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching from רבא about storage vessels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wine tank becomes usable by scalding.

steps.title: רבא sealed his empty kegs so no one could put wine in them
steps.stepSummary: When sending empty kegs to הרפניא, רבא turned them upside down in their sacks and sealed the sacks.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבא sent kegs to הרפניא, he turned them over onto their openings and sealed the sacks at their brims.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells what רבא used to do in practice. It sets up the reason, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Turning the kegs mouth-down and sealing the sacks made sure the gentile carriers could not pour wine into them on the way. Even a short use would cause a problem, as the next step explains.

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא כִּי הֲוָה מְשַׁדַּר גּוּלְפֵי לְהַרְפַּנְיָא,
phrases.english: Rava, when he would send kegs to Harpanya,
phrases.notes: הרפניא is the name of a town. The kegs were empty.

phrases.english: would turn them over onto their openings
and seal them at their brims.
phrases.notes: He sealed the sacks the kegs were packed in, so no one could get at the openings.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא כִּי הֲוָה מְשַׁדַּר גּוּלְפֵי לְהַרְפַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבא's own careful practice with storage vessels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא made sure his empty kegs could not be used for wine even briefly.

steps.title: Anything that holds wine for storage, even briefly, is under the decree
steps.stepSummary: רבא's reason: the rabbis' decree covers any storage vessel, even if the wine was stored in it only for a short time.
steps.simpleTranslation: He held: anything that takes in wine for storage, even just for a while, the rabbis made a decree about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבא was so careful with his kegs. This closes the section with a general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a short stretch of storage counts as קיום, so the vessel would become forbidden. That is why רבא blocked the carriers from using the kegs at all.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two levels. Items that only touch wine briefly (a ladle or funnel) can be wiped, according to רבי. Items that hold wine for storage (קיום) are forbidden, even if they held it only for a short time.
steps.confusionAlert: "For a short time" does not mean that brief contact is enough. The key word is still storage: the wine sits inside the vessel, even if only for a short while.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical test for which vessels need more than wiping: did the vessel ever hold the wine in storage, even briefly?

phrases.english: He held: anything that takes it in for storage,
even only for a while,
the Rabbis made a decree about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רבא's practice in step 24.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Any vessel that holds wine for storage, even for a short time, falls under the rabbis' decree.

steps.title: What material is used to wipe the vessels?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what one uses to do the 'wiping' (ניגוב) of a gentile's winepress and vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: With what does one wipe them clean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question: the משנה says to 'wipe' the winepress and vessels, but with what? This question opens a new topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives the rule that wiping is enough, but it does not say what material to use. The גמרא wants that detail filled in before moving on.

keyTerms.meaning: Wiping, the cleansing method the משנה requires

phrases.english: With what does one wipe them clean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבא's rulings about storage vessels and returns to the משנה's word 'wiping' to clarify it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What material is used to perform the wiping of a gentile's wine equipment.

steps.title: Water or ashes: two opinions
steps.stepSummary: רב says one wipes with water. רבה בר בר חנה says one wipes with ashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says: with water. רבה בר בר חנה says: with ashes.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question. רב says water is used, and רבה בר בר חנה says ashes are used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first glance this looks like a simple disagreement, with each one naming a different material. The next step will question whether they really disagree at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Ashes, used as a scrubbing agent

phrases.english: Rav says: With water.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר: בְּאֵפֶר.
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana says: With ashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: בְּמַיִם, רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר: בְּאֵפֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב: wiping is done with water. רבה בר בר חנה: wiping is done with ashes.

steps.title: Does each one exclude the other material?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רב really means only water and not ashes, and whether רבה בר בר חנה really means only ashes and not water. It then says 'rather' to set up its explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said water. Does that mean water and not ashes? רבה בר בר חנה said ashes. Does that mean ashes and not water? Rather...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges reading the two opinions as excluding each other. The last word, 'אלא' ('rather'), is the gate to the גמרא's answer, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking each opinion at face value creates a problem: it seems unlikely that one would use water but never ashes, or ashes but never water. So the simple reading of 'water' versus 'ashes' cannot be right. The גמרא is about to explain how the two statements really fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: With water and not with ashes?

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not deciding between רב and רבה בר בר חנה here. It is questioning the idea that each one rejects the other's material. The real explanation begins with 'אלא'.

phrases.english: Rav said: With water.
With water and not with ashes?

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר בְּאֵפֶר —
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said: With ashes.
With ashes and not with water?
Rather,

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַיִם וְלֹא בְּאֵפֶר? בְּאֵפֶר וְלֹא בְּמַיִם?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the simple reading of the two opinions given in step 27, and sets up a reinterpretation.
steps.kashyaTarget: The face-value reading that רב requires only water and רבה בר בר חנה requires only ashes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It makes no sense that either material would be excluded, so the two statements cannot simply mean 'only water' and 'only ashes'. The word 'אלא' signals that a new reading is coming.
